content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.75 and price is rising); model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.5) — model fails to account for downward pressure.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in correcting downward trends; true prices often dip below forecast by 1–3 days after sentiment shifts negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, especially when sentiment is high and price spikes — forecast peaks too early.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; adjust downward by 1–2% per day after sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is mixed or declining, model ignores structural downward momentum — true prices often drop faster than forecasted.
